summary: Accepted. The sealed twenty-two-operation candidate makes exactly the twenty initially audited repairs plus two classified posthumous receptions. It removes dated life assertions from mourning, retrospective, and posthumous contexts; keeps the Last Emperor's independently witnessed AD 923 death while classifying the AD 937 head reburial as a reception; removes the textual omen's fabricated regnal-year value; and retains the two source-directed upper bounds without invented lower endpoints.

sourceEvidence.reason: Qian Chuanjing's resumption explains that he was mourning his mother. It does not date the mother's life to the February AD 920 appointment.

reviewedChanges.reason: The candidate retains an undated relationship/death-before-mourning attestation and removes the unsupported AD 920 life hint.

sourceEvidence.reason: The clause recalls the prior rebellion as the cause of Yanzhou's longstanding suffering; the contemporaneous AD 920 context does not date Zhang Shoujin's life or revolt.

reviewedChanges.reason: Replacing the point date with an undated retrospective attestation is conservative and preserves the source claim.

sourceEvidence.quote: 北齊文士魏收著《後魏書》，於時自魏太武之初
sourceEvidence.reason: The 921 Historiography Office memorial discusses Wei Shou's earlier writing and describes its historical span from Northern Wei Taiwu; neither author nor ruler participates in the 921 memorial.

reviewedChanges.reason: Both records correctly retain undated historiographical references while removing invented personal AD 921 dates.

sourceEvidence.reason: The Last Emperor retrospectively calls on his deceased father/predecessor. The May AD 921 edict is not a life attestation for that former emperor.

reviewedChanges.reason: The candidate preserves the undated familial-retrospective evidence and removes only the false AD 921 life date.

sourceEvidence.quote: 晉天福二年五月，詔太社先藏唐朝罪人首級，許親屬及舊僚收葬
sourceEvidence.reason: The AD 937 edict concerns severed heads already stored at the Grand Altar, not living people.

sourceEvidence.quote: 詔左衛上將軍安崇阮收葬焉
sourceEvidence.reason: The order is collection and burial of the already-dead Last Emperor's head.

reviewedChanges.reason: The candidate removes the AD 937 life/death containers and reader hint, retains the independently witnessed AD 923 death, and adds one correctly classified posthumous reburial reception.

sourceEvidence.quote: 瑱字，一十一，十月一八日
sourceEvidence.reason: The text gives graph-splitting omen language.

sourceEvidence.quote: 析「王」字為「一十一」，析「真」字為「十月一八」
sourceEvidence.reason: The editorial note explicitly identifies the numerals as character analysis, not calendar data.

sourceEvidence.quote: 果以一十一年至十月九日亡
sourceEvidence.reason: This omen-fulfilment wording cannot independently create a regnalYear 11 or converted death date.

reviewedChanges.reason: Removing the omen-derived death container prevents a fabricated regnal-year field while leaving the separate AD 923 death evidence intact.

sourceEvidence.quote: 故左衛上將軍齊奉國贈太傅
sourceEvidence.reason: 故 identifies Qi Fengguo as already dead, and 贈 records the AD 920 posthumous honor.

reviewedChanges.reason: The candidate removes the impossible AD 920 life attestation and retains the visible dated honor as a posthumous reception.

sourceEvidence.reason: This gives the June AD 920 narrative anchor.

sourceEvidence.quote: 先是，河中朱友謙襲陷同州，節度使程全暉單騎奔京師
sourceEvidence.reason: 先是 makes Cheng Quanhui's flight earlier than that June entry, not a point event in AD 920.

reviewedChanges.reason: The source wording and on-or-before AD 920 bound preserve the direction without introducing a lower endpoint.

sourceEvidence.reason: This supplies the March AD 923 anchor.

sourceEvidence.quote: 先是，繼韜父嗣昭為潞州節度使，戰歿於鎮州城下
sourceEvidence.reason: The father Li Sizhao's death predates the March entry; it is not life activity in AD 923.

reviewedChanges.reason: The candidate correctly changes the point date to an on-or-before AD 923 bound and separates the earlier AD 920 commander hint from the later death-bound hint.
